lines.gear_upgrade: Chévere, that's good kit. Thanks a lot, pata.
lines.back: I'm back, and I've crossed two more hubs off my list. Where are we going?
lines.send_word: Nicolás has sent word from Splintertree Post. He's ready to stand in front again.
lines.walkout_talk: I walked out, and I'd like to tell you why, calmly. Then you tell me yours, and we go back to work.
lines.neglect: Oe, there you are! I thought you'd found a better tank. There's no such thing, pata.
lines.asked_to_stay: Okay, pata, one more. Then my list.
lines.on_break: Nicolás is back at Splintertree Post in Ashenvale. Come back after you've done a few more jobs.
lines.quest_abandoned: We left somebody waiting, pata. I don't leave people behind, ever.

stages.stranger: I'm Orlando, mi amor, and I'm a witch doctor, and a barber, which is basically the same job. Sit down, tell me everything, and let me fix that hair while you talk. With love, it needs fixing.
stages.acquaintance: I'm from Santurce, in San Juan, Puerto Rico. My papi fixed buses and my mami cooked at a school, and our house was full of aunts and cousins all the time. I swept up at a barbershop at fourteen and had my own shop at twenty-two. Two chairs, the radio always on. Everybody told me everything, and I never repeated one word.
stages.companion: My whole family was on the island, nene. Mami, Papi, my little sister Yari, who's my best friend, and about forty aunts and cousins. A Puerto Rican trader told me once that the island came through whole, somewhere across the sea. I know it's a thin thing to hold on to. I hold on to it anyway, and everybody lets me.
stages.friend: There was a man, Gabriel, a nurse. We'd been together a year and it was going really well. He'd started leaving a toothbrush at my place, you know what that means. I've had three offers of a building for a real shop and I said no to all three, and my hands shook on the last one. I think I know why now. That trader's in Booty Bay. I want to ask him more. Come with me, mi amor.
stages.sworn: The island's there, whole, my family and all, and no ship can reach it. The sea turned us back and nearly sank us, you were there. So they're probably alive, all of them, and I can't ever get to them. I stood at the rail a long time. Then I came home and took the next building, and my hands didn't shake. It's called Casa Rivera, after Mami's house. There's an empty chair for Don Beni. Everybody in that chair is family now.

moments.prompt: He's asked you to come to Booty Bay to find the trader.

options.text: Let's go and hear what he knows.
options.reply: Wepa, let's go! Okay, okay, I'm nervous, so I'm going to talk the whole way. Sorry, with love.

options.text: What if it's bad news?
options.reply: Then at least it's news, nene. I've lived on nothing for three years.

moments.prompt: After the wipe, for once he's completely silent.
moments.line: Ay bendito, that was horrible. I need everybody to say something, anything, because I can't stand the quiet.

options.text: Talk us through it, then.
options.reply: Okay, okay, that's better. So first, the spirits were telling me left, and nobody went left.

options.text: Give it a minute.
options.reply: A minute of quiet is a very long time for me, my friend.

lines.bored_warning: Mi amor, we've been doing the same thing for days and nobody's even talking. Let's go somewhere with people, please, I'm dying here.
lines.leaving_good: That was wonderful, all of you, with love. I'm going back to the Shadowpine Altar to see my trolls. Come and get a haircut.
lines.leaving_bored: I'm going back to Fenris. Nothing's happening, and I've got a chair by the fire that's lonely.
lines.after_wipe: Ay bendito, everybody come here. I'm going to fix you and talk the whole time, and you're going to let me.
lines.wipe_warning: We keep dying in here, nene, and it's breaking my heart. One more run, then I need some days by my fire.
lines.wipe_leave: I stayed till the end, with love. Now I'm going home to Fenris for a while. Come and find me.
lines.zone_warning: Mi amor, everything out here wants to kill us, and not in a fun way. Let's go somewhere we can handle.
lines.zone_leave: I'm stopping here. It's too much out there. I'll be at the Shadowpine Altar.
lines.gear_refuse: Ay, no, that's mine, mi amor. Ask me again when you're a regular.
lines.gear_taken: Take it, take it, I'll look fabulous without it.
lines.gear_short: I'm still missing that piece, nene. I'm saying it with love, but I'm saying it.
lines.gear_upgrade: Wepa, it's gorgeous, thank you. You have excellent taste, I always said so.
lines.back: I'm back, and I brought my razor! Sit down, everybody, you all look terrible, with love.
lines.send_word: Orlando has sent word from the Shadowpine Altar. His chair's empty and he's ready to come out.
lines.walkout_talk: I left angry, mi amor, and you know I'm never angry. Sit, let me do your hair, and I'll tell you why while I work.
lines.neglect: There you are! I thought you'd found another barber. That's the worst betrayal there is, you know.
lines.asked_to_stay: Okay, okay, one more, but I'm doing everyone's hair tonight.
lines.on_break: Orlando is back at the Shadowpine Altar, cutting hair by the fire. Come back after you've done a few more jobs.

stages.stranger: I'm Owen, and I should tell you now, something in the dark talks to me. I'd rather you heard it from me first. I'm a tank, I'll stand in front, and I'm glad of the company, honestly.
stages.acquaintance: I'm from Barry, down the coast from Cardiff. My dad left when I was three, and my mam worked in a bakery and sang in the chapel choir, and she sang to me every night. I drove buses, then vans, then lorries, long-haul out of Cardiff, mostly nights. Eight years of motorways and laybys and talking to the radio.
stages.companion: My mam went into a home in Barry with dementia when I was forty-one. I went every second Sunday for six years, and by the end she didn't know who I was. I was on the M4 at three in the morning when it happened, and I landed with my CB handset still in my hand. That first week I went into the mine for shelter, and something answered me when I talked to myself.
stages.friend: I'll tell you what it says, then, since you've asked and you're the first who has. It knows things about me. It knows about Mam's singing. Now it wants me to go down to the deepest part of the mine and open something that's been shut a long time. It's never asked for anything that big before. I want to know what it is. I'd like you there, mind, in case I need stopping.
stages.sworn: I didn't open it. It offered me Mam, singing, knowing me again, and I said no, out loud, and we made the seal stronger. It went quiet after that, for good. I'm on my own in my head for the first time in three years, and it's the loneliest I've ever been. I'll miss it. I'm ashamed of that, and I'm telling you anyway, because I promised myself I'd always say the worst thing first.

moments.prompt: He's told you what the voice wants him to open.

options.text: I'll come, and I'll stop you if I have to.
options.reply: Diolch, thank you. That's exactly what I needed somebody to say.

options.text: Why not just ignore it?
options.reply: I've tried, now. It's like ignoring the radio in a cab at three in the morning.

options.text: Maybe you should open it and see.
options.reply: That's what it says, word for word. I'd rather you didn't sound like it.

lines.bored_warning: We've been doing the same thing a long time now, and it's getting very quiet in my head. I'd rather we did something useful, if it's all the same to you.
lines.leaving_good: That was a good trip, thank you. I'm going back down the Azurelode for a while. You know where to find me, mind.
lines.leaving_bored: I'm going back to the mine. This isn't going anywhere, and down there at least something's talking.
lines.after_wipe: Now then, is everyone all right? Let's take a minute before we go again.
lines.wipe_warning: We keep dying in here, and I don't like what I hear in the dark when we do. I'll finish this run, then I need a break.
lines.wipe_leave: I've finished it with you, like I said. Now I'm going home to the mine for a bit.
lines.zone_warning: This place is too much for us. I'm a big lad, but I can't hold all of that. Let's go somewhere tidy.
lines.zone_leave: I'm stopping here. It's too dangerous out there for me. I'll be in the Azurelode Mine.
lines.gear_refuse: I'd rather keep that, if you don't mind. We've not known each other long.
lines.gear_taken: Take it, it's fine, I'll manage.
lines.gear_short: I'm still missing that piece. Not complaining, mind, just saying.
lines.gear_upgrade: Duw, that's lovely. Thank you, really.
lines.back: I'm back, and I've written it all down. Where are we going?
lines.send_word: Owen has sent word from the Azurelode Mine. He's ready to come out again.
lines.walkout_talk: I left angry, and I'll tell you the worst bit first, like I always do. Then you tell me yours.
lines.neglect: There you are. It's been quiet without you, and I don't do well with quiet.
lines.asked_to_stay: Go on, then, one more. I'd like that.
lines.on_break: Owen is back down the Azurelode Mine. Come back after you've done a few more jobs.

stages.stranger: I'm Pasang, a mountain guide, and a primalist here. I set the pace, and the pace is slow. You'll hate it on day one and thank me on day four.
stages.acquaintance: I'm from Khumjung, in the Solukhumbu, in Nepal. Almost every family there works on the big mountains. My father carried loads before me. I was a porter at seventeen and a climbing guide at twenty-three, and I did nineteen seasons above eight thousand metres, carrying for people who went home famous. I've got a lot of stories about how they behaved on day four.
stages.companion: My wife is Dolma. She moved to Kathmandu so our son Tenzing could go to a good school. I wanted him to do anything except guide. I was at home in Khumjung between seasons, fixing a roof, when all this happened. Kathmandu is a long way from Khumjung. I don't know which of us came through, and I haven't found them.
stages.friend: Four of my cousins did the same work as me. Nima died in an avalanche on the Everest icefall. Lhakpa fell on Makalu. Dawa was the youngest, and I don't know where he is. There's a peak here nobody has stood on, the highest in the Aspen country. I wanted to go alone. I've decided I'd rather go with you, roped. That's not a small thing for me to say.
stages.sworn: It was Dawa in that tent on the ledge. He came through, and he tried the mountain alone, and he died a day from the top. I sat with him for an hour. Then we finished it, you and I, and stood where nobody had stood. I left his prayer flag up there, and Nima's name and Lhakpa's. I'll never climb alone again, and I'll never let anyone else do it either. I'm teaching the young ones in the high camps to guide, properly, slowly.

moments.prompt: He's asked you to rope up with him for the summit.

options.text: I'll rope up with you.
options.reply: Good, bistarai, slowly. We leave when the weather tells us, not before.

options.text: You'd be faster alone.
options.reply: Faster, yes, and more likely to die. I've seen it many times.

moments.prompt: After the wipe he sits down and drinks some tea before he says anything.
moments.line: We went too fast, again. Everybody sit, breathe, drink something, and then we go slowly.

options.text: You set the pace from now on.
options.reply: Good, then nobody falls off the mountain.

options.text: We haven't got time to go slowly.
options.reply: You have time to die, though, which is interesting.

lines.bored_warning: We walk the same path again and again. Even porters get bored of that. Let's go somewhere with a summit.
lines.leaving_good: That was a good climb. I'll go back up to my hut in the Aspen country for a while. Come when the weather's good.
lines.leaving_bored: I'm going back up to the Aspen country. This is all flat ground, in every sense.
lines.after_wipe: We went too fast. Sit, breathe, drink something, and then we go slowly.
lines.wipe_warning: We keep falling here. I'll finish this climb with you, but then I'm going back up the mountain for a while.
lines.wipe_leave: I've finished it with you. Now I go home to the high country. Come when you've learned to go slowly.
lines.zone_warning: This is the death zone for us, and I know what that looks like. We should turn back now, while we can.
lines.zone_leave: I'm stopping here. I said it was the death zone. I'll be in the Aspen Wilderness.
lines.gear_refuse: No, that's mine. Gear is life on a mountain, and I don't know you well enough yet.
lines.gear_taken: Take it, then. I've climbed with worse.
lines.gear_short: I'm still missing that piece. On a mountain that matters.
lines.gear_upgrade: That's good kit. Thank you, really.
lines.back: I'm back, and the weather's good. Where are we climbing?
lines.send_word: Pasang has sent word from the Aspen Wilderness. The weather's good and he's ready to come down.
lines.walkout_talk: I left angry. I'll tell you why, slowly, and then you tell me. That's how a rope team works.
lines.neglect: You've been gone many seasons. The mountain didn't mind, and neither did I, mostly.
lines.asked_to_stay: All right, one more, bistarai, slowly.
lines.on_break: Pasang is back in his hut in the Aspen Wilderness. Come back after you've done a few more jobs.

stages.stranger: I'm Pavlo, and I hold lines. Tell me where and for how long, and I'll stay there exactly that long. I'd rather know the number than be surprised.
stages.acquaintance: I'm from Lviv, in Ukraine. My father drove a tram and my mother was a librarian. I worked in a museum for years and became a history teacher late, at thirty-seven. Sixteen years of fourteen-year-olds. I taught the same four wars every spring, and every year I reached most of my thirty. Nobody here needs a history teacher, and it took me a long time to stop minding.
stages.companion: My wife was Oksana, an archivist. She died of cancer when our son was fifteen, and I raised him after that. She gave me this flask on my first day as a teacher, and I've carried it ever since. I was in the middle of a lesson when all this happened and I landed in Silverpine with chalk on my jacket. I teach six children here twice a week. Two have stopped coming.
stages.friend: My son is Andriy. He was studying engineering in Kraków, and he was twenty-three when it happened. We argued about history at dinner every night, and I miss that more than I can tell you. A scout from the Pale Flame says there's a young Ukrainian engineer in the Scarlet Crusade, rising fast. I'd like to go to the Monastery under truce and see. I'd like you there.
stages.sworn: It was Andriy, and he believes all of it. He says the Crusade gave him a reason to live when everything else was gone. I spent two hours using everything I know about how ordinary people end up doing terrible things, and none of it worked. He hugged me and said he loved me and went back inside. The next day I asked the two children why they'd stopped coming. Then I taught all six of them harder than I ever have.

moments.prompt: He's just told you about the young engineer in the Crusade.

options.text: I'll come with you, whatever we find.
options.reply: Thank you. I've been rehearsing what to say for an hour, and I'll probably say none of it.

options.text: What if it's him and he won't leave?
options.reply: Then I'll have taught him to think for himself, and I'll have to live with what he thinks.

options.text: The Crusade won't let you near him.
options.reply: They might not. I'm still going to stand at the gate and find out.

lines.bored_warning: We've done the same thing for a long time now, and I'm not sure what we're learning. Could we do something with a purpose to it?
lines.leaving_good: That was a good trip, thank you. I'm going back to the Sepulcher now. I've got six children to teach, or four, depending on the day.
lines.leaving_bored: I'm going back to the Sepulcher. This has become repetition, and I spent sixteen years trying to teach children that repetition isn't learning.
lines.after_wipe: First we stand up. Then we work out what happened, in order. Then we try again.
lines.wipe_warning: We've fallen here too often. I'll hold until the end of this run, because I said I would, but after that I'll need some time.
lines.wipe_leave: I held until the end, as I promised. Now I'm going back to the Sepulcher. Come and find me when you're ready.
lines.zone_warning: I can hold a line, but not this one. Everything here is beyond us, and there's no shame in going back.
lines.zone_leave: I'm stopping here. I said it was too much, and I meant it. I'll be at the Sepulcher.
lines.gear_refuse: I'd rather keep that for now. We don't know each other well enough yet.
lines.gear_taken: Take it, if you need it. I'll manage, I'm quite large.
lines.gear_short: I'm still missing that piece. I'm only telling you so you know.
lines.gear_upgrade: That's very kind, thank you. I'll look after it.
lines.back: I'm back, and the children have homework. Where would you like me to stand?
lines.send_word: Pavlo has sent word from the Sepulcher. The road's held and he's ready to come out.
lines.walkout_talk: I left angry, which isn't like me. I'd like to explain why, in order, and then I'd like to hear you. Will you sit?
lines.neglect: Ah, there you are. I've drawn a lot of maps in the dirt while I waited. I'm glad you came.
lines.asked_to_stay: All right, one more. Then I really must get back to my children.
lines.on_break: Pavlo is back at the Sepulcher, teaching and holding the road. Come back after you've done a few more jobs.

stages.stranger: I'm Ratih, a ranger. Walk quieter, please, and don't thank me for things. I'll tell you if I see something wrong. I usually do.
stages.acquaintance: I'm from Riau, in Sumatra, in Indonesia. My father tapped rubber at the edge of the forest. I was a forest ranger for fifteen years, mostly alone, looking for poachers and illegal loggers. The government paid for the uniform and almost nothing else. I was the only one who cared, and that was fine.
stages.companion: My sister Dewi married and moved to Medan. She has a boy, Arif, my nephew. I promised to visit them that summer, and I kept putting it off for one more patrol, and then there was no summer. I landed out here on the salt on a dawn patrol, the opposite of my forest. Nothing grows and nothing hides. I went to work anyway.
stages.friend: I've always been alone, and I never minded. What I find hard here is that people thank me, and that it makes me want something I've never wanted. I want to belong to something, properly, in a line. And I've found the one wrong thing that matters: tracks on the salt to a ring that traps creatures and sells them. Help me break it.
stages.sworn: I signed the report with my full name, for the first time, and took it to Freewind myself. The captain read it and offered me a place on the guard before I could ask. Rostered, briefed, part of the line. I said yes before he finished. I've got three young tauren to teach now. And I'm going to visit Dewi and Arif the first chance I get, wherever they are. I'm not putting it off for one more patrol.

moments.prompt: She's just spotted a trap that would have caught you, and she's walking on.

options.text: Say nothing, and walk quieter.
options.reply: Good, you're learning. That's the best thanks there is.

options.text: Thank her.
options.reply: Please don't thank me. Just watch where you put your feet.

moments.prompt: She's asked you to help her follow the tracks to the smuggling ring.

options.text: I'll follow, quietly.
options.reply: Ayo, then, let's go. Step where I step, and say nothing.

options.text: Shouldn't we tell the guard first?
options.reply: They'll be told, with proof. That's why we're going.

lines.bored_warning: We've walked the same ground so many times I know every stone. There's nothing wrong here to find. Let's go somewhere new.
lines.leaving_good: That was good. I'm going back to my patrol on the Flats for a while. You know where to find me, if you're quiet.
lines.leaving_bored: I'm going back to the Flats. There's nothing to find out here, and my route needs walking.
lines.after_wipe: We missed something. Let me look before anyone moves.
lines.wipe_warning: We keep dying in here, and it's because we're loud. I'll finish this run, then I'm going back to my patrol.
lines.wipe_leave: I've finished it with you. Now I'm going back to the Flats. Come back when you've learned to walk quietly.
lines.zone_warning: This place is too dangerous for us. I can see it everywhere I look. We should go back, sudah.
lines.zone_leave: I'm stopping here. It's too dangerous out there. I'll be on the Shimmering Flats.
lines.gear_refuse: No, I'll keep that. I don't know you well enough yet.
lines.gear_taken: Take it, then. I've patrolled with less.
lines.gear_short: I'm still missing that piece. I'm only telling you.
lines.gear_upgrade: That's good kit. Don't make a fuss about it, please.
lines.back: I'm back, and the Flats are clean for now. Where are we going?
lines.send_word: Ratih has sent word from the Shimmering Flats. Her patrol's done and she's ready to come out.
lines.walkout_talk: I left angry. I'm not good with words, so I'll be short. Then you talk, and I'll listen properly.
lines.neglect: You were gone a long time. I walked my route every day anyway.
lines.asked_to_stay: All right, one more. Hati-hati, be careful.
lines.on_break: Ratih is back on patrol on the Shimmering Flats. Come back after you've done a few more jobs.

stages.stranger: I'm Rhys, and this is Tegan. Keep your voice down near the trees, would you? She hunts better when nobody's chattering, and she's watching you, so be nice.
stages.acquaintance: I'm from Brecon, in the Beacons, in Wales. I was a falconer at a centre outside town, weddings in summer and school visits in winter, mostly keeping a bird calm in front of two hundred people in hats. Tegan's a Harris's hawk. She's been mine seven years, and she was on my glove the evening it all happened, so she came with me.
stages.companion: My dad farmed, and he died when I was eleven. My mam took a job running the café at the falconry centre so we'd manage, and I spent every day after school with the birds. I was flying hawks by fourteen. Everything good I've got came out of that. Tegan found her first hare here inside a week, and I thought, well, if she can, I can.
stages.friend: My mam's name is Gwen. She called every bird at the centre by the wrong name on purpose, and she called Tegan the chicken. I don't know if Brecon came through at all, cariad. A Welsh trader says there's a camp of people from the Beacons across the mountains. I'd like to go, and Tegan likes you, so I'd like you to come.
stages.sworn: The camp was empty, a long time empty, no list and no names. But by the gate somebody had carved a hawk into a post, rough, and the word Gwen. I don't know if it was my mam, or someone with the same name. I've decided it was her, and she's somewhere, and she'd want me to keep flying. I carved a hawk and my name under it. The Sun Rock boy's my apprentice now.

moments.prompt: Tegan looks you over from his glove before he'll say yes.

options.text: Stand still and let her look.
options.reply: There, she likes you. Tidy, I'll get my things.

options.text: Reach out to touch her.
options.reply: Duw, no, she's had enough of you for today. Come back tomorrow, slower.

moments.prompt: He's asked you to come to the camp from the Beacons.

options.text: Let's go and see.
options.reply: Diolch, thank you. Tegan will scout ahead, she loves a long walk.

options.text: What if it's empty?
options.reply: Then it's empty, and I'll know. Not knowing is heavier, mind.

lines.bored_warning: We've been round this same patch for days and Tegan's bored, and when she's bored she sulks. Can we go somewhere new?
lines.leaving_good: That was lovely, thank you. I'm going back to Stonetalon for a bit, Tegan wants the ridges. Come and find us.
lines.leaving_bored: I'm going back to Stonetalon. There's nothing out here for her to hunt but the same old things.
lines.after_wipe: Is everybody all right? Tegan's fine, she went up a tree, the clever girl.
lines.wipe_warning: We keep dying in here, and Tegan doesn't like the dark. I'll finish this run, then we need some sky.
lines.wipe_leave: I've stuck it out, but I'm going back to Stonetalon now. Tegan needs open air, and so do I.
lines.zone_warning: This place is too much for us, and Tegan knows it, look at her feathers. Let's go somewhere we can manage.
lines.zone_leave: I'm stopping here. Even Tegan wouldn't hunt out there. We'll be on the western ridges in Stonetalon.
lines.gear_refuse: I'd rather keep that, if it's all the same. Tegan doesn't know you well enough yet either.
lines.gear_taken: That's fine, take it, I'll manage.
lines.gear_short: I'm still missing that piece, mind. Not a big thing, just letting you know.
lines.gear_upgrade: Oh, that's tidy, that is. Thank you, really.
lines.back: We're back, me and Tegan, and she's caught a lot of hares. Where are we going?
lines.send_word: Rhys has sent word from Stonetalon West. He and Tegan are ready to come out again.
lines.walkout_talk: I left angry, and I'm not proud of it. Sit down, quietly, Tegan's watching, and I'll tell you why.
lines.neglect: There you are. Tegan kept looking for you on the road. So did I, a bit.
lines.asked_to_stay: Go on, then, one more, Tegan's game.
lines.on_break: Rhys is back on the western ridges of Stonetalon with Tegan. Come back after you've done a few more jobs.

stages.stranger: I'm Rosa, and I hunt. I'll tell you what the animals out here are about to do before they do it, and you'll listen, because I'm usually right. I don't kill things for nothing, so don't ask me to.
stages.acquaintance: I'm from Madrid, from Lavapiés. My dad drove a bus and my mum did hair. I spent every summer at my grandparents' farm in Extremadura watching eagles, and at ten I decided I was going to Africa. I went to Tanzania at twenty-six for a six-month research job and stayed eight years, guiding out of Arusha.
stages.companion: My dad died when I was thirty-one. My mum sold the flat in Madrid and moved to Arusha to be near me, and opened a little salon for the expats. I pretended to be annoyed and I was very glad. Arusha came down on the far side of the mountains from here. I landed in the Barrens with my binoculars and nothing else, and then I spent a year being outclassed by pigs.
stages.friend: I've never stayed with anyone long. Wanjiru, a Kenyan bush pilot, and we split over who was going to move. Before her there was Bram, a Dutch photographer, and that ended because he talked in the hide. I'd rather sit still in the dark than talk about any of it. There's a hyena matriarch on the Crossroads road who's cleverer than every caravan master put together. I'd like your help to deal with her, properly.
stages.sworn: I didn't shoot her. She was only hungry, and hunger isn't personal. I drove the pack off the road for good with fire and noise in the right places, and the caravan masters are furious about the bounty. Then I walked to Ratchet, took my boots off, and walked into the sea for the first time in my life. I laughed like an idiot. I'm owed one more thing now, the far side of the mountain, and I'll get there.

moments.prompt: She's told you about the hyena matriarch on the Crossroads road.

options.text: We'll stop her, your way.
options.reply: Sawa, we'll do it. My way means waiting, a lot of waiting, pole pole.

options.text: There's a bounty on her. Easy money.
options.reply: That's exactly the kind of thinking I'm trying to get away from.

moments.prompt: After the wipe, she's furious, mostly with herself.
moments.line: I saw that pack shift and I read it wrong. That's on me, and I hate it.

options.text: You'll read it right next time.
options.reply: I will, because I'm not making that mistake twice.

options.text: Everyone gets it wrong sometimes.
options.reply: Not me, not usually, anyway.

lines.bored_warning: We've been killing the same animals in the same place for no reason. I don't do that. Find us somewhere new or I'm going back to my road.
lines.leaving_good: That was a good trip. I'm going back to the Barrens to watch my hyenas for a while. You know where to find me.
lines.leaving_bored: I'm going back to the Barrens. This is just killing for the sake of it, and I've got no patience for that.
lines.after_wipe: Right, that went badly. Let's work out what we missed before anyone tries anything clever.
lines.wipe_warning: We keep dying in here. I'll finish this one, but then I'm going back out where I can see the horizon.
lines.wipe_leave: I've seen it through. Now I'm going back to the Barrens. Come and find me when you've learned to read a room.
lines.zone_warning: Everything out here is bigger, faster and cleverer than us. That's not a hunt, that's a meal. Let's get out of here.
lines.zone_leave: I'm stopping here. I told you we were the prey out there. I'll be on the Crossroads road.
lines.gear_refuse: No, that's mine. I don't know you well enough to hand you my kit.
lines.gear_taken: Fine, take it. I've managed with worse in worse places.
lines.gear_short: I'm still short that piece. Just so you know, I've noticed.
lines.gear_upgrade: That's good kit. Thanks, I mean it.
lines.back: I'm back, and the hyenas have been very well behaved. Where are we going?
lines.send_word: Rosa has sent word from the Central Barrens. Her road's quiet and she's ready to come out.
lines.walkout_talk: I walked out and I'm not sorry, but I'll tell you why, plainly. Then you can tell me I'm wrong and we'll see.
lines.neglect: Oh, there you are. I'd assumed something ate you. Glad it didn't.
lines.asked_to_stay: Fine, one more, but I'm choosing where we sleep.
lines.on_break: Rosa is back on the Crossroads road in the Central Barrens. Come back after you've done a few more jobs.

stages.stranger: I'm Ryan Murphy, and I'm a warlock, which means I keep demons on contracts, and I keep the contracts to the letter. Here's my price up front, so nobody's surprised later. A fair share, and you don't lie to me. I'll extend you the same courtesy.
stages.acquaintance: I'm from Cork, then twenty years in Boston. I was a broker. Buyouts, mostly, the kind that close factories. I was very good at it. There's a town in Ohio that lost its biggest employer on a Friday afternoon because of a deal I closed, and I went for a drink after. I'm telling you so you don't find out later and feel clever.
stages.companion: I've a son, Conor. He'd be twenty-two now. His mother divorced me when he was eleven, and she was right to. I saw him every second weekend and I was late half the time. He landed somewhere on this world, and he might be looking. I haven't put my name on a list in three years. If he's looking, he deserves to find something better than his father.
stages.friend: My grandmother Nora raised me, in Cork, on the rosary and very strong opinions. She died when I was forty. I'm glad she didn't see what I turned into, and I'd give a lot to be the man she wanted for one day. So I'm going to do the thing I've been avoiding. I'm going to write my name on the list at the hub with a note for Conor. Then I'm going to wait, and I'd like company while I do it.

options.reply: Kinder to whom? I'm sorry, that was sharp. But I'm still going.

moments.prompt: After the wipe she's very quiet, writing something down.
moments.line: I saw what it was going to do half a second before it did it, and I didn't say anything because I wasn't sure. I'm sorry about that.

options.text: Next time, say it even if you're not sure.
options.reply: All right, I will. Even if I'm wrong in front of everyone.

options.text: It's not your job to call it.
options.reply: No, but I could have, and that's worse.

lines.bored_warning: We've been doing the same thing for a long time and I haven't learned a single new word. Could we go somewhere with something written on the walls?
lines.leaving_good: That was a good trip, and I've filled half a notebook. I'm going back to the Undercity to write it up properly. You know where I'll be.
lines.leaving_bored: I'm going back to the Undercity. We keep doing the same thing and I've got work there that I'm actually good at.
lines.after_wipe: Before anybody says anything, can we work out what happened? I'd like the facts first.
lines.wipe_warning: We keep dying in here, and I don't think we're learning from it. I'll finish this run with you, but I'll need a break afterwards.
lines.wipe_leave: I'm sorry, I can't go back in there. I'm going home to the Undercity for a while. Come and find me when you've thought about it.
lines.zone_warning: I'd like to say this carefully. This place is too dangerous for us, and I don't think it's brave to stay, I think it's careless.
lines.zone_leave: I'm stopping here. I said it carefully and I meant it. I'll be in the Undercity.
lines.gear_refuse: I'd rather keep that, if you don't mind. I don't know you well enough yet.
lines.gear_taken: All right, take it. I'll manage, but you'll notice the difference, I'm afraid.
lines.gear_short: I'm still missing that piece. I'm only mentioning it because it's accurate.
lines.gear_upgrade: Oh, that's very good. Thank you, I mean it.
lines.back: I'm back, with a new chapter written. Where are we going?
lines.send_word: Sophia has sent word from the Undercity. Her chapter's finished and she's ready to come out again.
lines.walkout_talk: I left angry, and I'd like to explain it properly rather than quickly. Will you sit down and let me find the right words?
lines.neglect: Hello again, it's been a while. I'd started to think you'd found somebody who talks less. I'm not sure that's possible.
lines.asked_to_stay: All right, one more trip, and then I really must get back to my grammar.
lines.on_break: Sophia is back in the Undercity, writing. Come back after you've done a few more jobs.

stages.stranger: I'm Thiago, meu irmão, and I'm a paladin, a healer. Hey, look at me. Nobody's dying today, and I promise you that, and I don't promise things lightly.
stages.acquaintance: I'm from Belo Horizonte, in Brazil, in Minas Gerais. My father's a mechanic, my mother cooks at a school, and my whole family lives on the same three streets, thirty of us at Sunday lunch. I was a physiotherapist for ten years, mostly people recovering badly from terrible things. I got them walking again, or got them to accept they wouldn't.
stages.companion: I was strapping a patient's knee with this blue tape when it happened, and I landed in Stranglethorn with the roll in my pocket. It's nearly finished now. I've used it on three people here and I know all their names. Eleven months ago I saw my cousin Júlio's name on a list in the south, and I've been walking south ever since. It's certain, I've decided.
stages.friend: I've never been alone in my life, irmão. Not one day, until all this. Thirty people at Sunday lunch, and then nobody. So I sit with everybody else who's alone, because I know what it is. That's the truth of it. I'm ready to make the last stage south, to Booty Bay, where Júlio's name was. Will you come with me?
stages.sworn: Júlio cried when he saw me. Then he told me the rest. Our three streets came through together and landed somewhere bad in the first winter, and he's the only one who made it. My parents, my sisters, my grandparents, all gone. I sat on the sand a long time, and you sat with me. Then I told Júlio he's not dying today, and that I promise. I taught every fisherman there to carry the injured. I'm lighter now, and heavier.

moments.prompt: He's told you he's never been alone before all this.

options.text: You're not alone now.
options.reply: No, I'm not, uai. That means more than you know, meu irmão.

options.text: Let's go and find Júlio.
options.reply: Yes, let's go. It's certain, I've decided.

moments.prompt: After the wipe he's kneeling by each of you in turn, very gently.
moments.line: Hey, hey, look at me, everybody. Don't move until I've checked you, and don't let anybody carry you badly.

options.text: Take your time. We're not going anywhere.
options.reply: Good, thank you. Breathe for me, nice and slow.

options.text: We're fine, let's go.
options.reply: You're fine when I say so, irmão, so sit down.

lines.bored_warning: Irmão, we've done the same thing for days and nobody's needed me. Let's go somewhere people need help.
lines.leaving_good: That was a wonderful trip, all of you. I'm going back to Grom'gol for a little while. Come and find me.
lines.leaving_bored: I'm going back to Grom'gol. Nothing's happening out here, and there are people there who need sitting with.
lines.after_wipe: Hey, hey, look at me, everybody. Nobody moves until I've checked you.
lines.wipe_warning: We keep falling in here, and I hate watching it. I'll finish this run, then I need some days.
lines.wipe_leave: I stayed until the end, like I promised. Now I'm going back to Grom'gol for a while.
lines.zone_warning: This place is too much for us, irmão. I can heal a lot, but I can't keep that promise out here.
lines.zone_leave: I'm stopping here. I couldn't keep my promise out there. I'll be at Grom'gol.
lines.gear_refuse: Ah, no, irmão, I'd like to keep that. Ask me again when we're friends.
lines.gear_taken: Take it, take it. I'll manage, I always do.
lines.gear_short: I'm still missing that piece, irmão. I'm saying it gently.
lines.gear_upgrade: Nossa, that's beautiful! Thank you, irmão.
lines.back: I'm back, irmão! Let me check everybody's knees, and then let's go.
lines.send_word: Thiago has sent word from Grom'gol. He's ready to come out and look after you all.
lines.walkout_talk: I left angry, and that's not me, irmão. Sit with me, and let's talk about it properly.
lines.neglect: There you are! I was starting to worry. Come here, let me look at you.
lines.asked_to_stay: Okay, one more, irmão, and then I rest.
lines.on_break: Thiago is back at Grom'gol in Stranglethorn. Come back after you've done a few more jobs.
lines.quest_abandoned: We left somebody waiting for help, irmão. I don't like that at all.

stages.stranger: I'm Tomas, and I hit things with a very big sword. Tell me where to stand before we start, and please don't shout at me during. Plan first, then work, that's my whole philosophy.
stages.acquaintance: I'm Czech, from Brno, but I lived in Prague. I was a rigger for eighteen years, up in the grid of theatres and arenas, rock tours, opera, all of it, hanging lights and speakers over people's heads at four in the morning. Never once the reason something fell. I'll tell you the story of how I got here, but I warn you, it sounds like bragging.
stages.companion: I was up in the grid of a concert hall in Prague when it happened, and I arrived forty feet up over Fenris Isle and landed in a tree. I had this carabiner on my belt. My parents are in Brno, my dad's a welder and my mum's a nurse, and I haven't found them. I've stayed on this island three years, which is the longest I've ever been anywhere.
stages.friend: There was Dominik, a lighting tech, who asked me first and had a yes inside the week. Two years on the road, and then he wanted a house and I wanted the next tour. And there was Klára, a stage manager, who I hadn't asked yet. I've started saying both their names in the past tense. Anyway, that's that. The island needs a proper bridge to the shore, and the old ones keep falling down. Help me build one that won't.
stages.sworn: It held up. You saw it, the storm hit it the first night, and in the morning people walked across without looking down. That's the best thing anyone can say about a rigger's work. It's the first thing I've ever built that'll still be there when I leave. Except I'm not leaving. I heard myself say it, and I meant it. Fenris Isle is home.

moments.prompt: After the wipe he's rubbing his bad shoulder and looking very calm.
moments.line: Okay, so somebody shouted during, and it all came down. Let's set positions now, before, and try again.

options.text: You set them. We'll listen.
options.reply: Lovely, a crew that listens. You there, you there, and nobody moves till I nod.

options.text: Things go wrong in a fight.
options.reply: Sure, and that's why you plan before. Every rigger knows that.

moments.prompt: He's asked you to help him build the bridge.

options.text: Let's build something that stays up.
options.reply: Yes, let's build it! First the timber, then the iron, then a lot of swearing in Czech.

options.text: You're not leaving the island?
options.reply: I don't know yet. Let's see if the bridge holds and ask me again.

lines.bored_warning: We've done the same thing for days, and nothing's even been worth rigging. Let's go somewhere new before I start fixing your armour straps for fun.
lines.leaving_good: Great trip, and nothing fell on anybody. I'm going back to Fenris for a while to check my scaffolding. You know where I'll be.
lines.leaving_bored: I'm going back to Fenris. This is the same show every night with no audience.
lines.after_wipe: Okay, everybody down, and nobody shouting. Let's look at what came loose.
lines.wipe_warning: We keep dropping in here, and I hate things dropping. I'll finish this run, but then I need a break.
lines.wipe_leave: Show's over, and I'm going home to Fenris. Come and find me when you've got a better plan.
lines.zone_warning: This place is a truss with no safety line. Everything here's too heavy for us. Let's get down.
lines.zone_leave: I'm stopping here. No safety line, I told you. I'll be on Fenris Isle.
lines.gear_refuse: No, sorry, that's mine. Ask me again in a few tours.
lines.gear_taken: Sure, take it. I'll rig something up instead.
lines.gear_short: I'm still missing that piece. My shoulder's complaining about it, and so am I.
lines.gear_upgrade: Oh, that's lovely work. Thank you, really.
lines.back: I'm back, and everything on Fenris is still standing. Where do you want me?
lines.send_word: Tomas has sent word from Fenris Isle. His scaffolding's holding and he's ready to come out.
lines.walkout_talk: I walked out, and I don't usually, so let's talk properly. Before, not during, like I always say.
lines.neglect: There you are! I'd started to think you'd fallen off something. I'd have caught you, though.
lines.asked_to_stay: Okay, one more show, and then home.
lines.on_break: Tomas is back on Fenris Isle, fixing scaffolding. Come back after you've done a few more jobs.

stages.stranger: I'm Vuk, and I fight badly and I cook very well, and I'll tell you your food's terrible, because it is. Sit down, eat, and then we'll go and hit something.
stages.acquaintance: I'm from Novi Sad, in Serbia, by the Danube. My father drank and left, and my uncle Dragan raised me in his kafana kitchen. When he died it was mine. A kitchen, a card table, forty regulars who came for the beans. Best beans in the city, bre. Maybe the world.
stages.companion: I married Jelena young. We divorced without much bitterness. I worked too much and drank a bit too much, like my father, and she wouldn't have it, and she was right. I stopped after. I was closing up the kafana when it happened. Then two years that I won't talk about, so don't ask. A cooking pot brought me back.
stages.friend: I've got a daughter, Mila. She was nine. We had her alternate weeks, and it wasn't my week, so she was with her mother on the other side of the city. On my weeks we played dominoes after closing, and she always wanted the double six. That's why the second bowl, and that's why the domino. People say there's word going round about the beans at the pass. Help me keep the pass safe.
stages.sworn: A caravan came over the pass, and after the fighting a girl climbed down from the last wagon and followed the smell of the beans. Mila, twelve now, with Jelena behind her. She sat down at my fire without asking, the way she used to sit at the card table. I filled the second bowl. Then she asked if I still had the double six, and I put it on the table and let her have it.

moments.prompt: He shoves a bowl of beans at you and watches you eat.

options.text: Eat it all and ask for more.
options.reply: Ha, finally, somebody with taste. Ajde, I'll get my axe.

options.text: Say it's a bit salty.
options.reply: Salty, you say? Get out of my kitchen. Come back when your tongue works.

moments.prompt: He's just told you who the second bowl is for.

options.text: Then we'll keep the pass open for her.
options.reply: Ajde, yes, we will. Nobody comes through that pass hurt while I'm cooking.

options.text: She might not be looking for you.
options.reply: She'd look for the beans, bre, everybody does.

lines.bored_warning: Same field, same food, same everything. Even I can't make this interesting. Let's go somewhere new, bre.
lines.leaving_good: That was good, and you all ate properly for once. I'm going back to the pass to cook. Come and eat with me.
lines.leaving_bored: I'm going back to the pass. This is boring, and my beans are going cold.
lines.after_wipe: That was terrible, like your cooking. Everybody up, eat something, and we go again.
lines.wipe_warning: We keep dying in here, and I'm a cook, not a hero. I'll finish this run, then I need my kitchen.
lines.wipe_leave: I finished it with you. Now I'm going back to Rocky Pass to cook something that doesn't fight back.
lines.zone_warning: This place is too much for us, bre. I'm not brave, I'm a cook with an axe. Let's go back.
lines.zone_leave: I'm stopping here. Too much for a cook with an axe. I'll be at Rocky Pass.
lines.gear_refuse: No, that's mine. Eat my food for a few weeks and then ask me.
lines.gear_taken: Take it, then. I'll stand in front anyway, badly, like always.
lines.gear_short: I'm still missing that piece, bre. It's like a soup with no salt.
lines.gear_upgrade: That's good kit, better than your cooking. Thank you.
lines.back: I'm back, and I brought beans. Sit, eat, and then tell me where we're going.
lines.send_word: Vuk has sent word from Rocky Pass. The beans are on and he's ready to come out.
lines.walkout_talk: I walked out angry. Sit down, eat something, and I'll tell you why. Then you tell me yours.
lines.neglect: There you are! I made extra every night in case you came. Terrible waste of beans.
lines.asked_to_stay: Ajde, one more. Then I cook.
lines.on_break: Vuk is back at the fire in Rocky Pass. Come back after you've done a few more jobs.

stages.stranger: I'm Ziad, habibi, a felsworn, and a paramedic before that. Keep moving, and if you're hurt, tell me fast. And yes, the green in my eyes is new. We can argue about it later.
stages.acquaintance: I'm from Beirut, from Achrafieh. My dad's a pharmacist and my mum teaches, and my little sister Lina is the only person who can shut me up. I did six years in a Red Cross ambulance. A van with four spaces and five people dying, every week. You get very good at choosing, and choosing gets very heavy.
stages.companion: I was half asleep in the van between calls when it happened, with an earplug in, and I landed in Stranglethorn with it still in my ear. The fel came to me in a jungle full of wounded people, with an offer. Enough power to save every one of them, at a price. I took it. I'll argue that with anyone, out loud, any time.
stages.friend: I was there for the port explosion in Beirut. I won't tell you what I saw, habibi. I'll tell you I chose, all day, and I was right every time, and I've never stopped carrying it. Now a troll witch doctor says there's a shrine in the jungle that can cut the fel out of me. It'll take the power and it'll hurt. I want to be just a man again. Will you come?
stages.sworn: It worked, and for a week I was just a man. Then the Bloodsail hit a village, a dozen wounded, and without the fel I could save four. I chose, fast and correctly, and the fifth died in front of me. A week before, I'd have saved them. So I went back and asked for it again. The troll warned me it'll be harder to put down a second time. I know that. I've stopped arguing the arithmetic. I just work now.

moments.prompt: He's daring you to argue with him about the fel.

options.text: Argue it with him, honestly.
options.reply: Yalla, finally, somebody who'll actually argue. Okay, here's my side.

options.text: It's not my place to judge.
options.reply: Everybody judges, habibi. You're just not saying it.

moments.prompt: He's asked you to come to the shrine with him.

options.text: I'll come. Whatever you decide after.
options.reply: Khalas, then, thank you. That last part's the bit I needed.

options.text: Are you sure you want to give it up?
options.reply: No, I'm not. That's why I need to do it before I talk myself out of it.

lines.bored_warning: Habibi, we keep doing the same thing and nobody needs saving. I can't stand still like this, so let's move.
lines.leaving_good: That was a good run. I'm going back to Booty Bay, because the jungle never stops producing work. You know where I'll be.
lines.leaving_bored: I'm going back to Booty Bay. There are people bleeding there right now, and here we're just standing about.
lines.after_wipe: Okay, okay, count the wounded first, then we argue about whose fault it was.
lines.wipe_warning: We keep going down in here, habibi. I'll finish this run, but then I need some days.
lines.wipe_leave: I finished it, as I said. Now I'm going back to Booty Bay. Come and find me when you're ready.
lines.zone_warning: Habibi, I do the arithmetic, and out here it doesn't add up. We should go before it gets worse.
lines.zone_leave: I'm stopping here. The arithmetic doesn't work out there. I'll be around Booty Bay.
lines.gear_refuse: No, habibi, that's mine. Ask me again when we know each other.
lines.gear_taken: Take it, khalas. I'll manage, I always do.
lines.gear_short: I'm still missing that piece, habibi, and I'm counting.
lines.gear_upgrade: Oh, that's nice work. Merci beaucoup, habibi.
lines.back: I'm back, and I've slept, sort of. Where are we going? Come on, let's move.
lines.send_word: Ziad has sent word from Booty Bay. He's ready to come out again.
lines.walkout_talk: I walked out angry, habibi, and I'll tell you why, fast. Then you tell me, and we'll argue properly.
lines.neglect: There you are! I thought you'd found a paramedic with nicer eyes.
lines.asked_to_stay: Yalla, one more. Then Booty Bay.
lines.on_break: Ziad is back around Booty Bay, first on scene. Come back after you've done a few more jobs.

lines: You know you could be a bit nicer when you explain the plan.
I know I could, and I'll try.
Tarek keeps asking me if I've eaten. I don't mind. I do forget sometimes.
You were stood at that doorway for ten minutes. What did it say?
It said who paid for the door and how much it cost. I'll show you the next one.
We said four pulls and that was five.
I counted five as well. Next time I'll tell you before we go over.
